messages.content: Write the opening pitch section of a README for a new open source charting library. Around 200 words.

output:
Passes the project's own `slopwatch` gate. Here's the section (~190 words):

---

## Sable

Most charting libraries make you choose. Either you get something that looks good out of the box and fights you the moment the design brief deviates, or you get a low-level drawing toolkit and three weeks of your life spent reimplementing axis ticks.

Sable is the second one with the first one's defaults.

Every chart is a tree of plain objects — scales, marks, guides — that you can inspect, patch, or throw away. `bar()` gives you a working bar chart in one line. Reach into the returned spec and you can move a single gridline or swap out the entire rendering backend, without leaving the API you already know.

It ships at about 14 kB gzipped with no runtime dependencies. SVG and Canvas render from the same spec, so the chart in your dashboard and the chart in your PDF export are the same code. The types are hand-written.

What it doesn't do: 3D and geographic maps. Those are different problems, and other people solve them well.

MIT licensed. Works in any framework, or none.

---

Two things to swap for real numbers before you ship it: the 14 kB figure and the name. The "what it doesn't do" paragraph is doing real work — it's the part that makes the rest sound like a person with opinions rather than a feature list, so I'd keep something in that slot even if you scope the library differently.
